## Overview

Deploy multi-agent graphs from a single prompt (planner-generated nodes and connections, parallel wave execution, shared state) and build the 3-layer context engineering stack (global rules, project knowledge, task state) with persistence across sessions. Exposed as A2A skills, MCP tools, runtime skill handlers, and example plugins.

## Authentication

All requests require a valid Bearer token or session cookie. Obtain a token via `POST /api/auth/login` or configure `REQUIRE_API_KEY=false` for local development.

## Graph Engineering (multi-agent graphs)

One prompt deploys a whole agent mesh: a planner model generates the graph
(nodes = agents with role prompts, edges = shared-state connections), the
engine validates it (cycles, unknown edges, caps) and executes independent
nodes in parallel waves. Every completed node writes its output into the
shared state; every dependent node reads the state of all its upstream nodes,
so agents reconcile contradictions instead of breaking.

### A2A skill `graph-engineering`

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:20128/a2a \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "message/send",
    "params": {
      "skill": "graph-engineering",
      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Research, draft, and review a migration plan for our SQLite → Postgres move"}],
      "metadata": {"model": "auto", "maxNodes": 15}
    }
  }'
```

Metadata options: `graph` (pre-built spec — skips planning), `planOnly: true`
(return the planned spec without executing), `model` (default node model,
`"auto"` routes via Auto-Combo), `plannerModel`, `maxNodes` (2–40).

### MCP tools

| Tool                             | Scope                 | Purpose                                  |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `omniroute_agent_graph_plan`     | `execute:agent-graph` | Prompt → validated graph spec            |
| `omniroute_agent_graph_validate` | `read:agent-graph`    | Cycle/edge/cap validation + waves        |
| `omniroute_agent_graph_run`      | `execute:agent-graph` | Plan (if needed) + execute, shared state |

Every node call runs through `/v1/chat/completions` with the
`x-omniroute-no-memory: true` header (disables memory/skill injection on
internal node requests — the recursion guard) and carries an
`x_agent_graph: {graph, node}` body marker that the `agent-graph-trace`
example plugin records as per-graph JSONL traces.

## Context Engineering Stack (3 layers)

| Layer   | Content                              | Persistence (memory type) |
| ------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| global  | identity, hard rules, constraints    | procedural                |
| project | architecture, conventions, decisions | semantic                  |
| task    | current goal, files, state           | episodic                  |

Layers assemble in fixed order (global → project → task) with a token budget
that trims task sections first and never drops the global layer. Persisted
sections are stored through the memory subsystem (key prefix
`context-stack:<layer>:<slug>`, UPSERT on re-save) so they survive between
sessions: load at session start, update at session end.

### A2A skill `context-stack`

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:20128/a2a \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "message/send",
    "params": {
      "skill": "context-stack",
      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Implement the export feature"}],
      "metadata": {
        "action": "build",
        "includeSaved": true,
        "sections": [{"layer": "global", "title": "Rules", "content": "Never touch src/payments/"}]
      }
    }
  }'
```

Actions: `build` (assemble; the user message becomes the task layer), `save`
(persist `metadata.sections`), `load` (return saved sections; filter with
`layers`). `apiKeyId` scopes persistence (default `a2a-context`).

### MCP tools

| Tool                            | Scope                 |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `omniroute_context_stack_build` | `read:context-stack`  |
| `omniroute_context_stack_save`  | `write:context-stack` |
| `omniroute_context_stack_load`  | `read:context-stack`  |

## Other surfaces

- **Runtime skill handlers** `agent_graph_run` and `context_stack_build`
  (registered at boot) — create a DB skill row whose `handler` names one of
  them to let models invoke these through the skills framework.
- **Example plugins**: `examples/plugins/context-stack` (injects the layered
  context as a system message on every chat request) and
  `examples/plugins/agent-graph-trace` (JSONL shared-state traces per graph).
- Deep dive: `docs/frameworks/GRAPH_ENGINEERING.md`.
